video_title: Jimmy Butler or Paul George 👀, Jalen Brunson speaks out and how VALUABLE are coaches 👀

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on his role and mindset for the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I'm filling J.J. Barea's role. He came off the bench for Dallas, he did all these great things.
quotes.quote: My mindset was just to be, I'm filling J.J. Barea's role. He came off the bench for Dallas, he did all these great things. That's where I see myself. I'm going to work to be better, but that's where I see myself, that's where I feel like I can help this team. And then the more you show in your role, the longer your leash gets, and the more you're able to do. People just want to say, 'Hey, I can do this, I can do that.' Well, do what's asked of you first, perfect it or master it, and all of a sudden you'll be surprised of what they allow you to do.

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on the importance of team-first play
quotes.excerpt: Finish your plate of food and then ask for more. That's my mindset.
quotes.quote: Finish your plate of food and then ask for more. That's my mindset. They set the table, they put the food out there for you. Finish your food and then when you prove that your plate is clean and clear, ask for more. That's how it is. It's simple as that. I always evaluated my teams and looked at what the team needed and said, 'Okay, I'm going to fulfill these roles because this is what we need.' I went to Indy, we had in the starting unit four of the scorers. Okay, I got to do all the shit that's in between the four of the scorers, which is rebounding, playing defense, getting steals. That's what I realized that I had to be a Swiss Army knife every single night.

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on the Knicks' mindset for the new season
quotes.excerpt: We don't want to speak of the trophy, we don't want to talk about the trophy.
quotes.quote: We don't want to speak of the trophy, we don't want to talk about the trophy. We don't want to see the trophy. We want to come in with the same mindset if not even tougher mindset we had last year.

quotes.speaker: Ray Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Felton on the lack of respect for veteran players

text_blocks.speaker: Ray Felton
text_blocks.text: And I'm not saying this is how it is, but you don't see the level of respect no more into today's game with these guys. Like when I seen guys like him, it was like, 'Oh, that's OG. What's up, baby?' Now it's like you see these kids, they be on some... You know what I'm saying? Like it's like, you know what I mean, it ain't the level of respect that we have for them guys who did it before us, who paved the way. They don't have that same level because what they don't understand is that we the reason y'all getting 300, 400 million dollars right now.

text_blocks.speaker: Theo Pinson
text_blocks.text: We paid the way for y'all.

text_blocks.speaker: Ray Felton
text_blocks.text: We paid the way for y'all. You know what I'm saying? But they don't they don't they don't look at it like that. These kids now are just, they're a little different.

quotes.speaker: Ray Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Felton on the challenges of being a veteran backup

text_blocks.speaker: Ray Felton
text_blocks.text: But when you come in the league, somebody is already there established in this organization that is the guy. They paying all the money too, so they getting all the shots, the offense is running through them. How can you fit to get minutes so you can show that you can play basketball, you can show some of your your skills, how can you fit within this system? It might be a knockdown shooter, it might be a defender, it might be a playmaker. Whatever that is, you have to do it and like Jalen Brunson said, and master it. Then you figure out what's next once you do that.

text_blocks.speaker: Theo Pinson
text_blocks.text: But a lot of these guys come in like, 'Man, man, I can do more. I can do this, I can do that.' And it's like, you hear it, as players we hear it. We sit on the sideline, you know, we'll be on the sideline waiting to go back in the game or you come out the game or whatever the situation is, you hear dudes over there like, 'Man, man, I can do that, man. I can do this.' And it's like, you going to be out the league before you know it.
